comments.body: The mutex field is named `mu`; rename it to `inflightMu` so readers can tell which state it guards. This function now acquires it twice on two different paths, and a generic name makes the second acquisition easy to misread during a future refactor. Blocking on naming here because lock discipline is the whole point of the change.
Early return for in-flight payments is a reasonable optimisation and keeps the hot path short. Nothing to change.

Map writes under the write lock look fine as written. Emit a histogram of lock wait time on this path (for example inflight_lock_wait_seconds) so contention is visible in dashboards before it appears as checkout latency. Without it we cannot tell whether this refactor bought anything, which makes it hard to justify keeping.

Wrap the error from doRetry with context, for example fmt.Errorf("retry %s: %w", payment.ID, err), so callers and logs can distinguish retry failures from other errors on the same path without reading stack dumps.

output.summary: Refactors the retry path from a single broad lock to a read-check-then-write pattern, which should reduce contention when many payments are retried concurrently. The change is well scoped and readable. Suggestions are around naming, observability of lock contention, and error wrapping; none are blocking. Reasonable optimisation overall.
